key_insight: M^4World is a driving world model that can generate realistic future surround-view video and LiDAR together, while letting users interactively manipulate objects over long time horizons. Its key advance is combining multi-view, multimodal prediction with stable minute-long streaming.
problem_solved: Current driving world models struggle with two major issues: they cannot precisely control individual objects in the scene, and they often lose stability or realism when generating long sequences. This paper addresses both object-level controllability and long-horizon consistency for autonomous-driving simulation.
method: Generates synchronized future surround-view camera streams and LiDAR scans as a unified driving world model.
Supports interactive object manipulation, enabling fine-grained edits to scene elements during generation.
Uses a streaming generation framework designed for stable minute-long rollouts rather than short clipped predictions.
impact: This is useful for autonomous driving researchers and practitioners because it improves simulation realism, controllability, and temporal stability. It can help create richer training and testing environments for planning, perception, and decision-making systems.
visual_elements: A multi-view driving scene diagram showing six surround cameras plus LiDAR output
A before/after object manipulation illustration highlighting editable vehicles or pedestrians
A timeline strip showing minute-long streaming generation across frames
An architecture block diagram linking prompts, control inputs, video synthesis, and LiDAR synthesis
paper_title: M$^\text{4}$World: A Multi-view Multimodal Driving World Model for Interactive Object Manipulation and Minute-long Streaming
paper_authors: Ke Cheng, Hanqiao Ye, Lei Shi, Yahui Liu, Yunhan Shen
